sections.h2: Where is Casper and what is around it?
sections.html:
Casper is in east-central Wyoming on the North Platte River and is the county seat of Natrona County. The city sits at roughly 5,100 feet and covers about 27 square miles.

Interstate 25 is the main route in and out, approaching from the north and east, and US 20/26 runs near the airport on the west side. Casper-Natrona County International Airport has United Express and Delta Connection service. Several smaller communities touch the city limits, so a Casper address may sit in a different jurisdiction than you expect:

  • Mills
  • Evansville
  • Bar Nunn
  • Unincorporated areas such as Allendale, Dempsey Acres and Red Buttes

Before you list or sell, confirm whether your parcel is inside the City of Casper or in the county. That decides who issues permits and who enforces nuisance rules.

sections.h2: What is the history of Casper?
sections.html:
Casper began when the railroad reached the site in June 1888, and residents petitioned for incorporation in April 1889. The town took its name from Fort Caspar, which honored Lt. Caspar Collins, who was killed nearby in 1865.

Oil shaped the city. Casper's first refinery was built in 1895, the oil boom ran from about 1910 into the mid-1920s, and by 1922 the Midwest Refinery was described as the largest in the world by gasoline volume. The population jumped from 2,639 in 1910 to 11,447 in 1920.

Boom and bust followed. The Texaco refinery closed in 1982 and the Amoco refinery in 1991, and the population fell from 51,016 in 1980 to 46,742 in 1990.

sections.h2: What does the Casper economy look like today?
sections.html:
Casper is a regional center for banking, commerce and energy, and it also leans on healthcare, manufacturing and tourism. Oil, gas, mining and wind power are foundational sectors, according to the city's economic development partner, Advance Casper.

Casper Mountain, the Hogadon ski area and the North Platte River support outdoor tourism. The airport is Wyoming's only Foreign Trade Zone, and a Sinclair refinery operates in nearby Evansville.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a mean hourly wage of $28.93 in the Casper metro in May 2025, compared with $33.54 nationally. Here are the largest occupation groups it listed:

Energy and construction jobs make up a large part of local work, so a slowdown can strain an owner's budget. A missed payment can turn into a sale decision.

sections.h2: How does Casper's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Casper has long, cold, dry winters and hot, mostly dry summers, so heating systems and roofs take the most wear. The normal January high is 35.2 degrees Fahrenheit and the normal July high is 89.0.

  • Average annual snowfall is about 71.8 inches.
  • Average annual precipitation is 12.22 inches.
  • Highs reach 90 degrees on about 38 days a year.
  • Lows drop to 0 degrees on about 15 nights a year.

Snow can be extreme. In the storm of April 3 and 4, 2023, Casper recorded 26.7 inches of snow in a day and 37.4 inches over two days, both records. After a roof collapsed at a commercial building, the Natrona County building official listed warning signs for owners to watch: creaking, visible sagging, cracked or split wood members, cracks in walls and doors that pop open.

If your roof, ceilings or walls show any of those signs, a buyer's inspector will find them. A cash buyer who purchases as-is will still look at them, but you will not have to repair them before closing.

sections.h2: Does Casper have flood or burn scar risk?
sections.html:
Parts of Casper can see flash flooding, especially downstream from the slopes of Casper Mountain. On July 29, 2013, the National Weather Service issued a flash flood warning for the east side of Casper after heavy rain fell on a recent burn scar from the Sheep Herder Hill fire.

Several homes along the Clear Fork of Muddy Creek were damaged, and flooding was reported on East Second Street between Wyoming Blvd. and Hat 6 Road. Much of that day's rainfall came in about 20 minutes.

If your home is on the east side or near a creek, check flood maps and ask your insurer about coverage before a buyer's lender does. Tell a buyer about any past water problem up front.

sections.h2: What permits and code rules apply to Casper sellers?
sections.html:
The City of Casper requires building permits for most projects, and it has adopted the 2021 International Codes, including the building, residential, fire, plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes. Amendments are in Title 15 of the municipal code.

Small jobs have different rules. Sheds under 120 square feet do not need a building permit, and a fence not over 6 feet high needs a fence permit but not a building permit. Platforms and walkways not more than 30 inches above grade are exempt from the building permit, while taller decks likely are not.

The Code Enforcement Division handles nuisance complaints. Typical issues include:

  • Weeds and overgrowth
  • Litter and accumulated junk
  • Junk vehicles
  • Dangerous buildings
  • Recreational vehicle parking

The city notifies the owner or tenant first and asks for a correction. If the problem is not fixed, the case may be referred to Municipal Court. Residents file complaints through the Casper 311 online form.

sections.h2: When are Natrona County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Wyoming property taxes are due in two halves, with the first half payable by November 10 and the second half payable by May 10 of the following year. Paying the full amount by December 31 avoids interest and penalty on the first half under the statute.

Taxes still unpaid on May 11 are declared delinquent, and the county treasurer then demands payment. Natrona County offers an online payment portal that asks for your bill number, tax year, last name and total tax bill. The county's main office is at 200 N Center, Casper, and the phone is 307-235-9200.

Because the tax follows the property, an unpaid bill can surface at closing. Check your balance before you sign a contract. Our Wyoming property tax guide explains the appeal process.

sections.h2: What should Casper sellers know about the deed and sale price?
sections.html:
A deed for a Casper sale must come with a sworn statement of the full price and terms, and Wyoming law keeps that statement confidential. Under W.S. 34-1-142, the county clerk cannot record the deed until the statement is filed.

The statement is not a public record, and the county may use it only for statistical sales-price ratios. Transfers such as foreclosure sales and certain gifts between family members are exempt from the price disclosure.

For recording fees and procedures, call the Natrona County main office at 307-235-9200, since the county page we reviewed does not list the clerk's fees.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Casper homeowner?
sections.html:
A cash sale means we buy your house without a lender, so the sale does not hinge on a bank appraisal or loan approval. You share a few details about the home, we review them, and you decide whether to accept.

We buy as-is, with no commission and no closing costs charged to you, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down. This option can fit a house with an old roof, deferred repairs, a code enforcement notice, or an estate that needs to be settled. Call or text (424) 435-2326, or fill out the form on this page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Casper house with a code violation?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a house that has open nuisance or permit issues, and we buy as-is. If you list the home instead, expect buyers to ask about notices from the Code Enforcement Division and about any unpermitted work.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a deck or fence in Casper?
faqs.a: Usually yes for a fence, since a fence permit is required even when the fence is not over 6 feet high. Decks not more than 30 inches above grade are exempt from the building permit, but taller ones likely need one. Confirm with the Building / Inspection Division.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Natrona County?
faqs.a: Half is payable by November 10 and half by May 10 of the next year. Bills unpaid on May 11 are delinquent. You can pay through the Natrona County online portal.

faqs.q: Is my sale price public in Wyoming?
faqs.a: No. The sworn statement of price filed with the deed is confidential under W.S. 34-1-142. Certain transfers, such as foreclosure sales, are exempt from the statement.

faqs.q: Does heavy snow damage matter when selling in Casper?
faqs.a: It can. Casper averages about 71.8 inches of snow a year, and the April 2023 storm set records. Buyers' inspectors look for sagging, cracks and roof wear, and a cash buyer who purchases as-is does not require those repairs first.
